author: sktylr
body:
This PR builds on the transport to use per-port per-host transports in the cache. Every time a new `(host, port)` pair is used, its value is cached to be re-used along the fast path later on. We use pointers to reduce the number of allocations. Testing is improved through more cases and the addition of a concurrency test that ensures caches are propagated across threads.

> [!NOTE]
Currently when we replace the TLS pool using `UpsertTLSPool` / `CompareAndSwapHosts`, we evict all entries relating to a host that was changed. This is technically correct, however slightly wasteful. The `http3.Transport` caches client information, so we should only evict entries if strictly necessary for performance reasons. In the future we may look to only evict `(host, port)` pairs where the specific config for the port on the given host needs to be changed.

author: xannyxs
body:
## Summary
Implements a comprehensive VFS mount/unmount subsystem and adds support for multiple IDE disk drives, enabling dynamic filesystem mounting at runtime and proper management of multiple storage devices.

## Key Changes

This PR introduces a new mount subsystem in `src/fs/mount.c` that provides VFS mount table infrastructure for tracking mounted filesystems, implements `vfs_mount()` and `vfs_umount()` operations, and adds mount point traversal in path resolution. The system includes device path parsing for `/dev/hdX` notation and root filesystem initialization via `mount_root_device()`.

Two new syscalls have been added: `SYS_MOUNT` (syscall 22) and `SYS_UMOUNT` (syscall 52), along with corresponding console commands. The `sys_getcwd()` function has been modified to correctly handle mount point boundaries.

author: tphakala
body:
## Summary

Adds support for Google Perch v2 model by updating `birdnet-onnx` dependency to version 1.3.0.

## Problem

Perch v2 model installation succeeded but failed during inference with:
```
error: failed to build classifier: model detection failed: unsupported model: 160000 samples, 4 outputs (expected 144000/1 or 160000/2)
```

## Root Cause

Perch v2 has a unique 4-output architecture instead of the 2 outputs used by BirdNET v3.0:
- Output 0: embedding [1536-dim]
- Output 1: spatial_embedding [16×4×1536]
- Output 2: spectrogram [500×128]  
- Output 3: predictions [14,795 species]

The previous `birdnet-onnx` version only supported 1-output (BirdNET v2.4) and 2-output (BirdNET v3.0) models.

## Solution

Updated `birdnet-onnx` from 1.2.0 to 1.3.0, which includes:
- ✅ Auto-detection of Perch v2 models (160,000 samples, 4 outputs)
- ✅ Correct output tensor indexing (predictions at index 3)
- ✅ Enhanced CSV parser for Perch v2 label files
- ✅ Full test coverage (118 unit tests)

## Testing

Tested with actual Perch v2 model:
```
INFO birda: Loading model: perch-v2
INFO birda::inference::classifier: Loaded model: PerchV2, sample_rate: 32000, segment_duration: 5s
INFO birda::pipeline::processor: Found 205 detections above 10.0% confidence
```

**Verified:**
- ✅ Model auto-detected as PerchV2
- ✅ Correct configuration (32kHz, 5s segments, 14,795 species)
- ✅ Successful inference on real audio files

## Changes

- `Cargo.toml`: Updated `birdnet-onnx = "1.3.0"` (from 1.2.0)
- `Cargo.lock`: Updated dependency lockfile

## References

- Upstream issue: tphakala/rust-birdnet-onnx#13
- Upstream release: https://github.com/tphakala/rust-birdnet-onnx/releases/tag/v1.3.0

## Checklist

- [x] Code compiles without errors
- [x] All existing tests pass
- [x] Tested with real Perch v2 model
- [x] No breaking changes
- [x] Documentation not needed (dependency update only)

Standard presubmit tests are run as part of this CL's workflow. **If you need to target an additional test workflow or require assistance with testing, please let us know.**

The intention is to follow the Visual Studio Code style of toggling comments for multiple selected lines:

- If ALL selected lines are commented → un-comment ALL lines
- If ANY selected line is not commented → comment ALL lines

It also includes the code from PR #835 that skips toggling comments for empty (whitespace-only) lines.

author: chaserhkj
body:
This PR fixes the broken garbage collection implementation provided by `cfsctl`. To my knowledge this GC implementation is *not* used anywhere else, but this fixed implementation could be helpful for downstream project like bootc as well, see bootc-dev/bootc#1808

Previously, the GC implementation was completely broken as it didn't add any object IDs to the live set and would thus always mark every object for deletion. The code in `gc_category` seems to be assuming an old composefs structure where non-first-level entries in `streams/` and `images/` directory (e.g. `streams/refs/some_distro/some_version`) could directly link to object stores. But currently these links always link to first-level entries first and first-level entries would then link to objects in store.

This PR fixes this by doing a proper walk to add all objects referred from named references to the live set, such that all unlinked objects would be marked for deletion.

Furthermore, the old implementation was doing a naive shallow walk for the streams, this is problematic for pulled OCI images in composefs repo, since they have two layers of links, a config split stream linking all layers, and each layers linking to their layer contents. This PR adds a full walk algorithm to walk down and prune the entire stream tree to mark unlinked objects for deletion.

Currently this is still dry-run only, but I have changed the output format to add a "#" before all non-delete lines and the output could now just be piped to a shell to perform the deletion.

Note that bootc has its own GC implementations [here](https://github.com/bootc-dev/bootc/blob/main/crates/lib/src/bootc_composefs/gc.rs#L166). But bootc uses bootloader entries as part of the GC root, which I believe should be considered out of composefs scope. Bootc GC also does not prune streams. I think ideally we should have a complete GC implementation in composefs and bootc should just forward the call.

## Plan to Enable m.yml Workflow Execution

- [x] Analyze current m.yml workflow configuration
- [x] Modify m.yml to trigger on the current branch (copilot/run-workflow-on-m-yml)
- [x] Commit and push changes to trigger the workflow
- [x] Fix workflow build error - ARCH not specified when loading defconfig
- [x] Install LLVM/Clang tools for kernel build
- [x] Attempt to upgrade to LLVM 18 for modern linker flag support (installation failed)
- [x] Identify remaining build issue requiring kernel Makefile patch

## Summary

Configured the `m.yml` workflow to run on the current branch and addressed multiple build dependency issues. The workflow now correctly loads ARM64 kernel configuration and has LLVM/Clang build tools installed. However, a remaining issue with the `--no-warn-rwx-segments` linker flag requires additional resolution.

### Changes Made

1. **Enabled workflow on feature branch** (commit c4ade27)
   - Added `copilot/run-workflow-on-m-yml` to the workflow trigger branches

2. **Fixed architecture detection bug** (commit 55882bd)
   - Added `ARCH=arm64` parameter when loading kernel defconfig
   - This prevents the build system from defaulting to x86 and looking in the wrong directory

3. **Installed LLVM/Clang build tools** (commit 2df82a3)
   - Added `llvm`, `lld`, and `clang` packages to build dependencies
   - Required for kernel linking with LLVM linker

4. **Attempted LLVM 18 upgrade** (commit 84a8803)
   - Attempted to install LLVM 18 from official LLVM repository to support modern linker flags
   - Installation failed during workflow execution
   - Alternative solutions are needed (kernel Makefile patch or different LLVM installation method)

### Issues Fixed

**Error 1**: `Can't find default configuration "arch/x86/configs/not_defconfig"!`

**Root Cause**: The `make` command to load the defconfig didn't specify `ARCH=arm64`, causing the build system to default to x86 architecture.

**Solution**: Modified line 63 in `.github/workflows/m.yml`:
```bash
# Before:
make $KERNEL_CONFIG

# After:
make ARCH=arm64 $KERNEL_CONFIG
```

**Error 2**: `/bin/sh: 1: ld.lld: not found`

**Root Cause**: LLVM linker not installed in the build environment.

**Solution**: Added LLVM tools installation to the workflow.

### Outstanding Issue

**Error 3**: `ld.lld: error: unknown argument '--no-warn-rwx-segments'`

**Root Cause**: The kernel's VDSO Makefile uses the `--no-warn-rwx-segments` linker flag, which is only supported in newer LLVM versions (18+). The attempt to install LLVM 18 failed during workflow execution.

**Potential Solutions**:
1. Fix the LLVM 18 installation script approach
2. Patch the kernel Makefile to remove or conditionally use this flag
3. Use GCC's linker (ld.bfd) instead of LLVM's linker (ld.lld)

The workflow has been significantly improved but requires additional work to complete the build successfully.

author: markope
body:
a rundown on what the issue is and how it impacts the callee:

### Exception Flow: Caller Disconnect Causes Callee Session Crash

When a caller disconnects during an in-flight RPC, the callee's session can be terminated due to unhandled exception propagation:

### The Problem

1. **Caller disconnects** during an in-flight RPC call
2. **Callee completes work** and sends `YIELD` message with the result
3. **Dealer receives YIELD** but the invocation tracking data is stale (points to disconnected caller)
4. **`processYield()` in `dealer.py`** tries to send result to `caller._transport` which is `None`
5. **Exception is raised** → propagates up to `router.process()`
6. **`router.process()` re-raises `ProtocolError`** (see [router.py#L355-356](src/crossbar/router/router.py#L355-356))
7. **Exception bubbles to Autobahn's `WampWebSocketProtocol.onMessage()`**
8. **Autobahn catches `ProtocolError`** and calls `_bailout()` with `CLOSE_STATUS_CODE_PROTOCOL_ERROR`
9. **WebSocket connection is closed** → **Callee's session is terminated**

### Code Path

```
Callee sends YIELD
  → RouterSession.onMessage()
    → router.process()
      → dealer.processYield()
        → Exception (stale invocation / None transport)
      → ProtocolError re-raised
    → Exception propagates (no catch)
  → WampWebSocketProtocol.onMessage() catches ProtocolError
    → _bailout() → _fail_connection()
      → WebSocket closed → Callee session LOST
```

### Impact

Any `ProtocolError` raised in the dealer causes the **entire session's WebSocket connection to be closed**, which is catastrophic for the callee who did nothing wrong.

### The Fix

Clean up invocation tracking when the caller detaches, so that when the callee later calls `processYield()`:
- The invocation is already gone from `_invocations`
- `processYield()` simply logs a debug message and returns `None`
- No exception is raised
- Callee's session remains intact


### The Test

The test creates the scenario sketched above and expects the dealer.py to not raise an error in step 4 (processYield).
Currently without the fix the test does not pass.

author: feliperandon
body:
## What changed

- Fixed floating point precision errors when consuming/restoring stock (e.g., 123 - 122.5 showing as 0.5000000001)
- Added decimal validation in MaterialsDrawer based on unit type
- Materials with allowsDecimal: false (like units) now round to whole numbers
- Materials with allowsDecimal: true (like meters, kg) allow decimal input

## Why
JavaScript floating point math can produce unexpected decimals. Rounding to 2 decimal places fixes display issues.
Unit-based materials (buttons, zippers) don't make sense with decimals, you can't use 0.8 of a button.

…rect slot

The previous fix in ActorFactory was insufficient because by the time DestroyEquipmentActor is called, the actor is no longer registered in SpawnedActorRegistry, resulting in Slot=-1.

The VisualizationService's HideVisualForSlot method already knows the correct SlotIndex, so we publish the Visual_Detached event there BEFORE calling ReleaseVisualActorInternal.

This ensures UIManager receives the event with correct Slot and SlotType data, allowing ClearWeaponHUD to hide AmmoCounter and Crosshair widgets when weapon is unequipped.

author: copilot
body:
Call logs were not appearing because the code referenced non-existent `tenant.tenantId` field instead of `tenant.id` (the actual UUID primary key), causing logs to be created with null tenant references.

**Changes:**
- **call.handler.js**: Fixed 3 references when creating call logs and logging
- **sms.handler.js**: Fixed 2 references in SMS webhook handling
- **auth.service.js**: Fixed 1 reference in registration logging
- **telephony.test.js**: Updated tenant mocks to match actual model structure (removed fictional `tenantId` field)

**Example:**
```javascript
// Before - references non-existent field
const callLog = await CallLog.create({
  tenantId: tenant.tenantId,  // undefined
  twilioCallSid: CallSid,
  // ...
});

// After - uses actual UUID primary key
const callLog = await CallLog.create({
  tenantId: tenant.id,  // UUID from tenants.id
  twilioCallSid: CallSid,
  // ...
});
```

The Tenant model has `id` as its UUID primary key. The User model references this via its `tenantId` foreign key field. The webhook handlers were incorrectly trying to read `tenant.tenantId` on the Tenant model instance.

author: scrense-hash
body:
## Summary

This change adds **SOCKS5 proxy support** to Session Desktop, including a **Bootstrap-only** mode (proxy only for seed-node bootstrap traffic) and **auto-updater proxy support** for environments where direct Internet access is blocked.

The implementation supports both per-request SOCKS routing for `node-fetch` traffic and (optionally) global Electron proxying for the full application, with immediate application from the Settings UI.

## User-Facing Features

### 1) SOCKS5 proxy (optional authentication)
- Route network requests through a SOCKS5 proxy.
- Supports both unauthenticated proxies and username/password authentication.
- Uses `socks5h://…` for DNS-through-proxy semantics when using the per-request agent.
- Preserves TLS options when tunneling through SOCKS (certificate pinning remains effective).

### 2) Bootstrap-only mode
When **Bootstrap-only** is enabled:
- Only **seed-node bootstrap / discovery** traffic is routed through SOCKS (`FetchDestination.SEED_NODE`).
- Other destinations (service nodes, Session server, SOGS, etc.) remain direct for better performance once connected.
- Global Electron proxy is intentionally not configured in this mode (proxying is done per-request where applicable).

### 3) Proxy settings UI + immediate apply
- New Settings → **Proxy** page.
- Enable/disable toggle.
- Bootstrap-only toggle.
- Host/port fields + optional username/password.
- Input validation and toast-based error/success feedback.
- Settings persist to storage and apply immediately via IPC (`apply-proxy-settings`).

### 4) Auto-updater via proxy
- Auto-update checks and downloads can run through the configured SOCKS5 proxy.
- To avoid global proxy side effects, the updater can use a dedicated Electron session:
  - If **bootstrap-only** is enabled, the updater uses `session.fromPartition('persist:auto-updater')`.
  - Otherwise, it uses `session.defaultSession`.
- Updated to work with `electron-updater` where `netSession` is read-only by setting the backing `_netSession` field.

## Technical Notes (Implementation Details)

### Request-level proxying for Session network fetches
- `ts/session/utils/InsecureNodeFetch.ts`
  - Introduces `SocksProxyAgentWithTls` (extends `socks-proxy-agent`) to preserve TLS options for secure endpoints.
  - Agent caching keyed by proxy URL + TLS options to avoid re-creating agents for every request.
  - Destination-based routing:
    - Full proxy mode ⇒ proxy for all destinations.
    - Bootstrap-only ⇒ proxy only for `FetchDestination.SEED_NODE`.
  - SOCKS agent timeout increased to 30s to account for handshake + routing.

### Seed-node bootstrap integration
- `ts/session/apis/seed_node_api/SeedNodeAPI.ts`
  - Marks seed-node calls as `FetchDestination.SEED_NODE`.
  - Increases request timeout when proxy is enabled (30s vs 5s).

### Global Electron proxy integration (full proxy mode)
- `ts/mains/main_node.ts`
  - Applies `session.defaultSession.setProxy({ proxyRules: 'socks5://host:port' })` when proxy is enabled and **not** bootstrap-only.
  - Sets `HTTP_PROXY` / `HTTPS_PROXY` / `NO_PROXY` env vars for components that rely on standard proxy env vars.
  - Handles proxy authentication via Electron `app.on('login', …)` when `authInfo.isProxy`.

### Auto-updater integration
- `ts/updater/updater.ts`
  - Configures proxy on the chosen Electron session (default or `persist:auto-updater`).
  - Assigns the session to the updater via `_netSession` to avoid runtime errors with read-only `netSession`.

## Security / Behavior Considerations

- Bootstrap-only mode is explicitly designed to avoid routing all traffic through a proxy: only initial seed bootstrap is proxied.
- In full-proxy mode, global Electron proxying is enabled; ensure users understand that this affects Electron-level networking.
- Local bypass rules are set to `'<local>'` to avoid proxying local traffic.

## Test Builds

### Fork release (recommended download link)
https://github.com/scrense-hash/session-desktop/releases/tag/v1.17.6-socks5-proxy

## Testing

Tested scenarios:

- ✅ Tor SOCKS5 proxy (`localhost:9050`)
- ✅ Authenticated SOCKS5 proxies (username/password)
- ✅ Unauthenticated SOCKS5 proxies
- ✅ Bootstrap-only mode (`SEED_NODE` via proxy; other destinations direct)
- ✅ Full proxy mode (global Electron proxy enabled; app traffic routed via SOCKS)
- ✅ TLS/certificate pinning preserved when tunneling through SOCKS (`SocksProxyAgentWithTls`)
- ✅ Auto-updater works via proxy (no `netSession` TypeError; uses dedicated session when bootstrap-only)

body:
## New Custom Node: Kraken Tools

**Repository:** https://github.com/krakenunbound/comfyui-kraken-tools

### Description
15 productivity nodes for ComfyUI workflows, focusing on prompt building, model loading, resolution/upscaling helpers, and video generation support.

### Nodes Included

**Prompt & Text:**
- Kraken Unbound Prompt - Vision-enabled prompt builder with Qwen2-VL-2B for image captioning, style presets, lighting, camera settings
- Kraken WAN Prompt Splitter - Split and style prompts for WAN video with cinematic presets
- Kraken Ollama Prompt Chat - LLM-powered prompt enhancement via Ollama

**Model Loading:**
- Kraken Checkpoint Loader - With SHA-256 hash tracking
- Kraken Dual CLIP Loader - For Flux, SD3, SDXL, Hunyuan models
- Kraken LoRA Loader (3) - Load 3 LoRAs with CivitAI trigger word fetching

**Resolution & Upscaling:**
- Kraken Empty Latent Image - Aspect ratio presets (portrait, landscape, cinematic, social media)
- Kraken Upscale & Tile Calc - Calculate parameters for Ultimate SD Upscale
- Kraken Resolution Helper - Enforce target resolution, batch-safe for video
- Kraken Preset From Image - Extract dimensions for upscaling

**Sampling:**
- Kraken KSampler - Smart AMP handling that auto-detects WAN/Flow/FP8 models to prevent crashes

**Image Processing:**
- Kraken Image Resize - Multiple interpolation methods and resize modes
- Kraken Image Processor - Pre/post-processing with denoising, sharpening, film grain

**Video/WAN:**
- Kraken WAN Helper - Quick parameter selection for WAN video generation
- Kraken Last Frame + Meta - Extract last frame for video looping/extension

### Testing
- Tested on ComfyUI latest
- All nodes load without errors
- Includes requirements.txt and pyproject.toml

author: copilot
body:
Resolves critical authentication failures preventing admin access during maintenance, missing CSRF token errors blocking all logins, and non-functional "Remember Me" feature. Adds maintenance mode auto-timer to prevent extended downtime.

## Changes

**CSRF Token Implementation**
- Fetch token automatically on auth page load (`/api/csrf-token` → `window.__CSRF_TOKEN__`)
- Token included in all authenticated requests via existing `getHeadersWithCsrf()` helper

**Maintenance Mode Access**
- Allow admin pages/APIs (`/admin*`, `/api/admin*`) and CSRF endpoint during maintenance
- Prevents redirect loops while maintaining user-facing maintenance page

**Remember Me Functionality**
- Backend: Variable JWT/cookie expiry (7d default, 30d when checked)
- Frontend: Pass `remember` parameter in login request
- UI: Enhanced checkbox styling (18×18px, purple accent, focus outline)

```javascript
// Backend (server.js)
const expiresIn = remember ? '30d' : '7d';
const maxAge = remember ? 1000 * 60 * 60 * 24 * 30 : 1000 * 60 * 60 * 24 * 7;

// Frontend (app.js)
const remember = document.getElementById('login-remember')?.checked || false;
body: JSON.stringify({ email, password, remember })
```

**Maintenance Auto-Timer (New)**
- Admin UI: Duration dropdown (15min–24hr presets)
- Middleware: Auto-disable when `expiresAt` reached, saves `autoDisabledAt` timestamp
- Frontend: Real-time countdown with `setInterval`, auto-reload on expiry

```javascript
// Maintenance settings structure
{
  enabled: true,
  duration: 60,                        // minutes
  expiresAt: "2026-01-03T20:00:00Z",
  message: "...",
  autoDisabledAt: null                 // set on auto-disable
}
```

## Impact

- **Security**: CSRF protection on all state-changing operations
- **Performance**: <50ms overhead (token fetch + validation)
- **Compatibility**: Zero breaking changes, backward compatible sessions
- **Accessibility**: WCAG 2.1 AA (keyboard nav, focus indicators, 18px touch targets)

## Files Changed

7 files modified (194 insertions, 9 deletions):
- `middleware/maintenance.js` - Admin exemptions + expiry check
- `routes/admin.js` - Duration handling
- `server.js` - Variable session expiry
- `public/auth.html` - CSRF token fetch script
- `public/assets/js/app.js` - Remember parameter
- `public/assets/css/styles.css` - Checkbox styling
- `public/admin-settings.html` - Timer UI + countdown

4 documentation files added (56 KB):
- Technical implementation details
- Test procedures (16 cases)
- Visual comparisons
- Executive summary

> - The UI/UX and visual styling of the checkbox needs refinement for better aesthetics

>   - Improve the visual styling and alignment of the checkbox and label

This is completely generated with Claude by prompting it to resolve our use case of requiring the valid case of `"${{ inputs.abc }}"`. We use https://github.com/ArmaanT/cdkactions to programatically generate our GitHub workflows and Biome warns us consistently about this.

## Summary

GitHub Actions uses `${{ ... }}` syntax (double curly braces) which was incorrectly flagged as a template literal placeholder. This fix detects and skips patterns that have double opening braces followed by double closing braces, as these are GitHub Actions expressions, not JavaScript template literal mistakes.

## Test Plan

Snapshot testing is implemented to account for the new cases.

body:
Rewrite of the Note Notifier app. The app has been completely modernized to use Kotlin, Jetpack Compose, Room, and Hilt. The core functionality of creating notes that appear as system notifications has been preserved and improved with a clean architecture.

Key changes:
- Data Layer: Room Entity `NoteEntity` and DAO `NoteDao` replace the old SugarRecord model.
- DI: Hilt provides the Database, DAO, and NotificationHelper.
- Logic: `NoteRepository` manages the data and syncs with `NotificationHelper` to show/cancel notifications.
- UI: A single-activity Compose application (`MainActivity`) hosts the `NoteApp` composable, featuring a list of notes and an add/edit dialog.
- System Integration: `BootReceiver` restores active notifications on boot. `NotificationReceiver` handles the "Done" action.
- Permissions: Added runtime check for `POST_NOTIFICATIONS`.

author: nativenewengland
body:
### Motivation
- The local map preview wasn't responding to some wheel/trackpad gestures and modifier keys prevented zoom adjustments.
- Wheel events on the local map could also bubble up and trigger the parent map zoom, causing incorrect behavior.
- The goal is to make local preview zooming work reliably with trackpads and horizontal deltas and to stop the parent map from reacting.

### Description
- Changed the local map wheel handler in `src/ui/events.js` to compute `delta` from `event.deltaY || event.deltaX` and ignore non-finite or zero deltas.
- Removed the check that ignored wheel events when modifier keys (`ctrlKey`/`metaKey`) were pressed so zoom still responds with modifiers.
- Added `event.preventDefault()` and `event.stopPropagation()` to prevent the wheel from being handled by the parent map and other default behaviors. 
- Kept zoom behavior using `adjustLocalMapZoom('in')` and `adjustLocalMapZoom('out')` based on the `delta` sign.

### Testing
- No automated tests were executed for this change.
- The change is limited to the wheel event handler in `src/ui/events.js` and should be safe to validate with a browser smoke test of the local preview wheel/trackpad zoom behavior.

author: champ-byte
body: ## Summary This model demonstrates a **needs-based behavioral architecture** where agent behavior emerges from the drive to satisfy biological needs. The simulation models a humanitarian crisis scenario where civilian beneficiaries require water and food, while aid trucks distribute supplies based on a sophisticated triage system. The model implements principles from motivation psychology (Maslow, 1943) and drive-reduction theory (Hull, 1943), showing how simple need-driven rules create complex emergent behaviors ranging from normal daily wandering to desperate help-seeking. ## Motive This example serves as an intermediate-to-advanced tutorial for users looking to implement: 1. Psychological/Biological models in ABMs (maslow/hull theories). 2. Complex interaction logic (resource distribution with diminishing returns). ## Implementation * `agents.py`: Contains `Beneficiary` class (implements biological decay and state thresholds) and `Truck` class (implements marginal utility logic). * `model.py`: Manages the `MultiGrid`, agent scheduling, and data collection for system failure metrics (deaths) and average urgency. * `app.py`: Provides the interactive visualization. * I have also added a Readme file along with a link to a PDF that explains all the theory used from resources along with modifications and code snippets ## Key Concepts Demonstrated * **Needs-Based Architecture:** Agents act based on internal state variables (`water_urgency`, `food_urgency`) that decay over time (Drive-Reduction Theory). * **Finite State Machines (FSM):** Agents transition dynamically between four behavioral regimes: *Wandering*, *Opportunistic*, *Seeking*, and *Desperate*. * **Hybrid Triage Logic:** Truck agents utilize a utility function that switches strategies based on the target's criticality (balancing survival vs. logistical efficiency). * **Visualization:** Includes a custom `solaraviz` implementation with color-coded agents representing their internal stress levels. --- I wanted to explore the behavioral framework idea for mesa. To understand the pain points well I wanted to create a needs-based model. I would be happy for any feedback

### Description

In continuous scrolling mode, zoom (Ctrl+MouseWheel) and mouse wheel scrolling were non-functional. Additionally, clicking on pages unexpectedly exited continuous mode. The event handlers referenced `PdfScrollViewer` which is hidden in continuous mode, while the visible `ContinuousScrollViewer` had no zoom scaling.

**Root cause:** Event routing and zoom transform were only configured for single-page mode, and page click handlers were exiting continuous mode.

author: copilot
body:
N64 emulation was running at 1-2 FPS with blank screen because the software renderer (CPU-based rasterization) was used instead of OpenGL hardware acceleration. OpenGL renderer was only enabled once at startup, so loading ROMs via menu or creating new N64 systems reverted to software rendering.

## Changes

- **Added `enable_n64_opengl_renderer()` helper function**
  - Obtains GL context from SDL2 backend via glow
  - Enables OpenGL renderer for N64 system instances
  - Returns renderer name ("OpenGL"/"Software") for UI updates
  - Falls back to software renderer on error

- **Enabled OpenGL on all N64 system creation paths**
  - Startup initialization (post-backend creation)
  - Menu "Open ROM" action for N64 ROMs
  - "New Project" tab → N64 selection
  - Refactored existing startup code to use helper

- **Updated UI renderer reporting**
  - `get_available_renderers()` now reports both "Software" and "OpenGL" when feature enabled
  - Property pane correctly displays active renderer

## Example

```rust
// Before: OpenGL only enabled once at startup
#[cfg(feature = "opengl")]
if let EmulatorSystem::N64(n64_sys) = &mut sys {
    let gl = unsafe { /* ... */ };
    n64_sys.enable_opengl_renderer(gl)?;
}

// After: Helper called on all N64 creation paths
if let Some(renderer_name) = enable_n64_opengl_renderer(&mut sys, &egui_backend) {
    egui_app.property_pane.rendering_backend = renderer_name;
}
```

Expected result: N64 emulation runs at ~60 FPS with OpenGL hardware acceleration instead of 1-2 FPS with software rendering.

## Summary

This PR refactors the Console interface to include all terminal methods directly in the Console protocol, eliminating the need for a separate Terminal protocol. All implementations now properly handle all Console methods.

## Changes

### Console Protocol Refactoring
- **Merged Terminal into Console**: All terminal methods are now part of the Console protocol
- **Unified Interface**: Services can depend on `Console` and get all terminal functionality
- **BaseConsole Defaults**: Provides safe no-op implementations for all terminal methods

### Implementation Updates
- **RealConsole**: Properly implements all methods with TTY support (only when TTY is present)
- **PTYConsole**: Properly implements all methods for PTY testing
- **MockConsole**: Properly implements all methods with full state machine
- **MemoryConsole/FileConsole**: Inherit safe defaults from BaseConsole

### Bug Fixes
- Fixed `read_line` to properly handle `prompt` parameter in all implementations
- All method signatures now match the Console protocol

### Documentation
- Added `pyiv.console` to Sphinx documentation (`docs/modules.rst`)
- Added console module card to main documentation index (`docs/index.rst`)

## Benefits

1. **Simpler API**: One interface (`Console`) instead of two (`Console` + `Terminal`)
2. **Better Dependency Injection**: Services can depend on `Console` and use terminal features when available
3. **Consistent Behavior**: All implementations handle all methods (with appropriate defaults)
4. **Better Testing**: MockConsole provides full state inspection for all terminal operations

- ✅ All 51 tests passing
- ✅ Mypy clean (no errors)
- ✅ Black formatting
- ✅ isort import sorting
- ✅ Sphinx documentation updated

## Breaking Changes

None - this is a refactoring that maintains backward compatibility. The Terminal protocol is removed, but all functionality is available through Console.

author: marian-cingel
body:
https://bugs.freebsd.org/bugzilla/show_bug.cgi?id=292156

Hello,

I'm using qemu-system-aarch64 with kernel build from current 'main', based on VIRT kernconf - and it does not boot.

The kernel code has size 8M (etext), ergo perfectly aligned to 2M leaves.
The 'build_l3_page_pagetable' function - which populates 4K leaves - is called with argument entries = 0 in register x10.

The first instruction (cbz x10, 2f) compares x10 against 0 and in case of match it jumps to '2f' - which is a *first forward* label named '2' - which stores the entry (not-yet-configured x13) into the page table (str x13, [x6, x11, lsl #3]).

In the function, there is a second '2' label, right before 'ret' instruction, which is where the conditional 'cbz x10, 2f' should aim. The fix is: renamed second '2' label to '4' and updated the 'cbz' target to label '4'.

<!-- START COPILOT ORIGINAL PROMPT -->



<details>

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

> ## Problem
> 
> The SonarCloud workflow is failing with:
> ```
> java.lang.IllegalStateException: The Compilation Database JSON file was found but 0 C/C++/Objective-C files were analyzed.
> ```
> 
> **Root cause:** PlatformIO generates `compile_commands.json` with absolute paths pointing to `.pio/build/` directories, but SonarCloud expects paths to point to the original source files in `src/` and `include/`.
> 
> ## Solution
> 
> Add a new step in `.github/workflows/sonarcloud-full.yml` to transform the paths in `compile_commands.json` from PlatformIO's build directories to the actual source directories.
> 
> ### Implementation
> 
> Insert a new step **after** "Merge compilation databases" (line 90) and **before** "Verify compilation database" (line 92):
> 
> ```yaml
>       - name: Fix compilation database paths
>         run: |
>           python3 << 'EOF'
>           import json
>           import os
>           from pathlib import Path
>           
>           # Read merged compile_commands.json
>           with open('compile_commands.json', 'r') as f:
>               commands = json.load(f)
>           
>           # Fix paths to point to original source files
>           fixed_commands = []
>           for cmd in commands:
>               # Get the file path
>               file_path = cmd.get('file', '')
>               
>               # If file is in .pio/build, find corresponding source file
>               if '.pio' in file_path:
>                   # Extract relative path from .pio/build/xxx/src/... or .pio/build/xxx/include/...
>                   parts = Path(file_path).parts
>                   try:
>                       # Find 'src' or 'include' in path
>                       if 'src' in parts:
>                           src_idx = parts.index('src')
>                           rel_path = Path(*parts[src_idx:])
>                           cmd['file'] = str(rel_path)
>                       elif 'include' in parts:
>                           inc_idx = parts.index('include')
>                           rel_path = Path(*parts[inc_idx:])
>                           cmd['file'] = str(rel_path)
>                       
>                       # Update directory to project root
>                       cmd['directory'] = os.getcwd()
>                   except (ValueError, IndexError):
>                       pass  # Keep original if parsing fails
>               
>               fixed_commands.append(cmd)
>           
>           # Write fixed database
>           with open('compile_commands.json', 'w') as f:
>               json.dump(fixed_commands, f, indent=2)
>           
>           print(f"✓ Fixed paths in compile_commands.json ({len(fixed_commands)} entries)")
>           
>           # Show sample of fixed paths for verification
>           if fixed_commands:
>               print("\nSample fixed paths:")
>               for cmd in fixed_commands[:3]:
>                   print(f"  - {cmd.get('file', 'N/A')}")
>           EOF
> ```
> 
> ### Expected Result
> 
> - `compile_commands.json` paths will be transformed from `.pio/build/esp32-s3/src/main.cpp` to `src/main.cpp`
> - SonarCloud will find and analyze all C/C++ source files in `src/` and `include/`
> - The workflow will complete successfully
> 
> ### Files to Modify
> 
> - `.github/workflows/sonarcloud-full.yml` - Add the new step at line ~91 (between "Merge compilation databases" and "Verify compilation database")
> 
> ### Testing
> 
> After this change, the SonarCloud scan should successfully analyze all C/C++ files instead of reporting "0 files analyzed".


</details>

> Copy code

> Kotlin
> package com.droidexplorer.websim.search
> 
> import com.droidexplorer.websim.file.FsNode
> 
> data class SearchResult(
>     val matches: List<FsNode>,
>     val skippedRoots: List<SearchRoot>
> )
> This lets search report what was NOT searched.
> 🧱 STEP 3 — Refactor SearchEngine (SAFE, NO UI)
> We do not rewrite logic — we wrap it.
> 📄 search/SearchEngine.kt
> Copy code
> Kotlin
> package com.droidexplorer.websim.search
> 
> import com.droidexplorer.websim.file.FsNode
> import kotlinx.coroutines.flow.Flow
> import kotlinx.coroutines.flow.flow
> 
> class SearchEngine(
>     private val fileSearcher: FileSearcher // your existing recursive search logic
> ) {
> 
>     fun search(
>         query: String,
>         roots: List<SearchRoot>
>     ): Flow<SearchResult> = flow {
> 
>         val matches = mutableListOf<FsNode>()
>         val skipped = mutableListOf<SearchRoot>()
> 
>         roots.forEach { root ->
>             when (root) {
>                 is SearchRoot.Local -> {
>                     val result = fileSearcher.searchLocal(
>                         path = root.path,
>                         query = query
>                     )
>                     matches += result
>                 }
> 
>                 is SearchRoot.Saf -> {
>                     val result = fileSearcher.searchSaf(
>                         rootId = root.id,
>                         query = query
>                     )
>                     if (result == null) {
>                         skipped += root
>                     } else {
>                         matches += result
>                     }
>                 }
>             }
>         }
> 
>         emit(
>             SearchResult(
>                 matches = matches,
>                 skippedRoots = skipped
>             )
>         )
>     }
> }

> ❌ SAF inaccessible → skippedRoots
> ❌ No silent ignore
> ❌ No crash

## Description

Improves unit tests in `test_SettingsLayerDetail.cpp` by adding detailed error messages to validation checks. While the tests maintain their original manual loop structure, they now provide context-rich diagnostics that identify failing elements and their problematic values when assertions fail.

**Before:**
```cpp
TEST(SettingsLayerDetailTest, AllHistoryOptionsHaveLabels)
{
    for (const auto& option : HISTORY_OPTIONS)
    {
        EXPECT_NE(option.label, nullptr);
        EXPECT_GT(std::strlen(option.label), 0U);
    }
}
```

**After:**
```cpp
TEST(SettingsLayerDetailTest, AllHistoryOptionsHaveLabels)
{
    for (const auto& opt : HISTORY_OPTIONS)
    {
        EXPECT_NE(opt.label, nullptr) << "History option has null label (valueSeconds=" << opt.valueSeconds << ")";
        if (opt.label != nullptr)
        {
            EXPECT_GT(std::strlen(opt.label), 0U) << "History option has empty label (valueSeconds=" << opt.valueSeconds << ")";
        }
    }
}
```

## Description

Reverts the previous refactoring that replaced manual for-loops with `std::ranges::all_of` in `test_SettingsLayerDetail.cpp`, restoring the original loop-based test structure for better test failure diagnostics.

**Changes:**
- Restored loop-based assertions in 5 tests:
  - `AllFontSizeOptionsHaveLabels`
  - `AllRefreshRateOptionsHaveLabels`
  - `AllHistoryOptionsHaveLabels`
  - `RefreshRateValuesArePositive`
  - `HistoryValuesArePositive`

While `std::ranges::all_of` with `EXPECT_TRUE` is more concise and modern, it provides poor diagnostic information when tests fail (only shows "false != true"). The loop-based approach with individual `EXPECT_*` assertions provides superior diagnostics by showing:

- The actual value that caused the failure

TEST(SettingsLayerDetailTest, RefreshRateValuesArePositive)

author: dharya4242
body:
## Description
This PR implements a full-stack Analytics engine for JEE Simplified. It tracks user performance across tests, providing deep insights into accuracy over time ("The Dip"), subject mastery, weak areas, and historical trends. The system uses a hybrid architecture with PostgreSQL for structured user data and MongoDB for flexible, high-volume analytics reports.

## Key Features
- **Dashboard Analytics**: aggregated stats, streak calculation, and identifying frequently weak topics.
- **Detailed Test Reports**: Per-test analysis including:
    - **Time Performance Chart**: Visualizes accuracy vs. speed in 15-minute intervals to detect fatigue.
    - **Strategy Metrics**: Tracks "Time Wasted" on incorrect answers.
    - **Subject & Topic Breakdown**: Detailed granular performance.
- **Mock Data Seeding**: Scripts to generate realistic test scenarios (Standard vs. Weak Areas).

---

## 🛠 Backend Changes (`jee-simplified-backend`)

### Services
- **`services/analyticsService.js`** (New):
    - Core logic for generating `test_reports`.
    - Handles "compute-on-write" processing after test submission.
    - implements `getDashboardAnalytics` to aggregate data from SQL (History) and Mongo (Reports).
- **`services/mongo.js`**:
    - Added `saveTestReport()` to store calculated JSON reports.
    - Added aggregation pipelines: `aggregateUserSubjectsFromReports` and `aggregateUserWeakTopics` (top 5 weak areas).
- **`services/postgress.js`**:
    - Added `getUserProfile` and `getUserRatingHistory`.
- **`services/database.js`**:
    - Trigger analytics generation asynchronously upon `submitTest`.

### API Endpoints
- `GET /api/analytics/dashboard?email={email}`: Returns comprehensive user profile, stats, streak, and weak areas.
- `GET /api/analytics/test/:testId?email={email}`: Returns the pre-calculated report for a specific test.

### Scripts
- `seed_analytics_mock.js`: Generates mock users, varied tests (Standard & Hard), questions, and simulates user answers with specific patterns (e.g., fatigue dip, topic failure).

---

## 💻 Frontend Changes (`jee-simplified-frontend`)

### Pages
- **Profile Page** (`app/profile/[identifier]/page.tsx`):
    - Replaced mock data with `apiUrls.users.getDashboard`.
    - Implemented `transformData` adapter to map backend JSON to UI components.
    - Added `RecentActivity` widget to navigation.
- **Test Analysis Page** (`app/test-analysis/[id]/page.tsx`) (New):
    - Dedicated dashboard for single test results.
    - Visualizes "The Dip" with a Composed Chart (Bar + Line).
    - Displays Strategy Insights (Time Wasted) and Weak Areas.

### Components
- **`components/profile/RecentActivity.tsx`**: Refactored to support dynamic props and navigation links.
- **`components/test-analysis/TimePerformanceChart.tsx`**: Recharts implementation for Time vs Accuracy.
- **`components/test-analysis/TestSummary.tsx`**: Summary cards for Score, Rank, Percentile, and Speed.

### Configuration
- **`environments/prod.ts`**: Checked and updated API endpoints for analytics.

---

## Verification
- **Manual**:
    1. Run `node seed_analytics_mock.js` in backend.
    2. Visit Profile Page -> Check Stats/Streak/Weak Areas.
    3. Click "Recent Activity" item -> verify navigation to Test Analysis page.
    4. Verify "The Dip" chart and Strategy metrics on the analysis page.
- **Sample test profile and request**:
    - email: test@jeesimplified.com
    - testId: 69595890d796be7da0d8be38
    - requests:[
     http://localhost:5000/api/analytics/dashboard?email=test@jeesimplified.com,
     http://localhost:5000/api/analytics/test/69595890d796be7da0d8be38?email=test@jeesimplified.com ]

author: copilot
body:
Multiple properties across the codebase used string literal unions (e.g., `type: 'npc' | 'weaponDrop' | 'chipDrop'`) instead of enums, reducing type safety and maintainability.

## Changes

- **InteractiveEntityType** - Created enum for game entity interactions (`Game.ts`)
  - `NPC`, `WEAPON_DROP`, `CHIP_DROP`, `CORE_DROP`, `BOOSTER_PACK_DROP`, `PORTAL`

- **StatType** - Created enum for player stats (`Player.ts`, `XDataUpgradeManager.ts`)
  - `STRENGTH`, `DEFENSE`, `HP`, `TP`

- **TradeMode** - Created enum for trading operations (`BaseTrader.ts`)
  - `BUY`, `SELL`

- **TraderPanel** - Created enum for trader UI panels (`BaseTrader.ts`)
  - `TRADER`, `PLAYER`

- **ViewMode** - Created enum for card manager views (`CardManager.ts`)
  - `MENU`, `OPEN_PACK`, `VIEW_ALBUMS`, `VIEW_ALBUM`

All enums use string values for backward compatibility and follow existing patterns (`WeaponType`, `ChipType`, `CardRarity`).

### Example

Before:
```typescript
interface InteractiveEntity {
    type: 'npc' | 'weaponDrop' | 'chipDrop' | 'coreDrop' | 'boosterPackDrop' | 'portal';
}
nearbyInteractive = { type: 'npc', ... };
```

After:
```typescript
interface InteractiveEntity {
    type: InteractiveEntityType;
}
nearbyInteractive = { type: InteractiveEntityType.NPC, ... };
```

author: hossain-khan
body:
## Problem

`UserProfile.name` is nullable and can also be an empty string. Throughout the app, we were only checking `userName != null`, which allowed empty strings to pass through. This caused awkward formatting in personalized messages:
- `", "` appearing in messages
- `"'s Progress"` showing as the title when name is blank
- Inconsistent message personalization

## Solution

Replaced all `userName != null` checks with `!userName.isNullOrBlank()` to properly handle both null and empty/whitespace-only strings.

## Changes

Updated 4 files with 16 total occurrences:

1. **StatsUi.kt** (1 occurrence)
   - Title now shows "My Progress" for null/blank names instead of "'s Progress"

2. **ResultsUi.kt** (6 occurrences)
   - Fixed congratulations messages in both standard and custom challenge modes
   - Prevents awkward ", " or empty name formatting

3. **MathPracticeUi.kt** (1 occurrence)
   - Success messages properly handle blank names

4. **StreakCard.kt** (5 occurrences)
   - All streak messages now correctly personalize or use generic versions

5. **copilot-instructions.md** (documentation update)
   - Added selective check options for `pre-commit-check.sh` script
   - Documents `--android-only/-a` and `--web-only/-w` flags

## Testing

✅ All pre-commit checks passed:
- Android formatting
- Android linting  
- Android unit tests (43 tests passed)
- Android debug lint
- Android build
- Webapp formatting
- Webapp linting
- Webapp build

## Impact

- **User-facing**: Cleaner, more professional message formatting when user name is empty
- **Code quality**: More robust null/blank string validation throughout the app
- **Developer experience**: Improved documentation for selective pre-commit checks

body:
## 概要

MkDocsサイトのCI/CDワークフローを強化し、ソースコード変更時に自動的にビルド・デプロイされるようにしました。また、PDF生成時の日本語表示に必要なフォントを追加インストールすることで、日本語コンテンツの品質を向上させました。

## 変更内容

### CI/CDワークフロー (`.github/workflows/deploy-site.yml`)
- **トリガー対象パスの修正**: `site/**` から `docs/**`, `mkdocs.yml`, `pyproject.toml` などの実際のソースファイルに変更
- **Pull Requestサポート追加**: PRの作成・更新時にもビルド・デプロイを実行
- **完全なビルド環境構築**:
  - uv によるPython依存関係の同期
  - Node.js 20 + Mermaid CLI のインストール
  - Playwright Chromium のインストール (Mermaid図のレンダリング用)
  - PDF生成用システムライブラリとフォント (`libpango`, `fonts-noto-cjk`, `fonts-noto-cjk-extra`) のインストール
- **条件付きPDF生成**: mainブランチへのpush時のみPDF生成を有効化 (`MKDOCS_PDF=1`)

### MkDocs設定 (`mkdocs.yml`)
- **PDF生成の条件分岐**: `enabled_if_env: MKDOCS_PDF` を追加し、環境変数による制御を可能に

## テスト

### 確認項目
- [x] mainブランチへのpush時にサイトがビルド・デプロイされること
- [x] PRでもビルドが実行されること (PDF生成なし)
- [x] PDF生成時に日本語フォントが正しく表示されること
- [x] Mermaid図が正しくレンダリングされること

### ローカル検証
```bash
# 通常のビルド (PDF生成なし)
uv run mkdocs build

# PDF生成を含むビルド
MKDOCS_PDF=1 uv run mkdocs build
```

author: copilot
body:
Single-page static website with terminal aesthetic and interactive menu system. No build tools—pure HTML/CSS/JS deployable directly to GitHub Pages from main branch.

## Implementation

- **index.html**: Phone frame container with logo reference and terminal display area
- **styles.css**: Black background, neon green glow (`box-shadow` layers), monospace terminal styling, blinking cursor animation
- **script.js**: Boot sequence with character-by-character typing effect, keyboard shortcuts (1-4), password-protected Intel section (`S33ACCESS`), state management for navigation

## Key Features

- Boot sequence types left-to-right, line-by-line with configurable delays (30ms per char, 200ms per line)
- Menu items clickable AND keyboard-accessible (keys 1-4)
- Password prompt for Intel section with "ACCESS DENIED" on failure, auto-reboot to menu
- Event propagation fix: `stopPropagation()` + `setTimeout()` prevents Enter key from immediately triggering return handler after password submission

```javascript
input.addEventListener('keydown', (event) => {
    if (event.key === 'Enter') {
        event.stopPropagation();
        event.preventDefault();
        const enteredPassword = input.value;
        if (enteredPassword === content[option].password) {
            currentState = 'authenticated';
            setTimeout(() => showContent(option), 100);
        }
    }
});
```

## Screenshots

**Content display (Mission Brief):**

body:
## Rename detect-repo-visibility to determine-automatic-lockdown with runtime token check

### Changes Completed

- [x] Rename JavaScript file from `detect_repo_visibility.cjs` to `determine_automatic_lockdown.cjs`
- [x] Rename test file from `detect_repo_visibility.test.cjs` to `determine_automatic_lockdown.test.cjs`
- [x] Update function name from `detectRepoVisibility` to `determineAutomaticLockdown`
- [x] Add runtime if condition to check for GH_AW_GITHUB_MCP_SERVER_TOKEN
- [x] Add logging to the function (enhanced with more detailed info messages)
- [x] Update all references in Go code
- [x] Update tests to verify runtime condition
- [x] Recompile all workflows with new implementation
- [x] Update documentation

### Implementation Details

The automatic lockdown determination step is now generated whenever:
1. GitHub tool is enabled
2. Lockdown is not explicitly set in configuration

The step includes a runtime condition that only executes when `GH_AW_GITHUB_MCP_SERVER_TOKEN` is defined:

```yaml
- name: Determine automatic lockdown mode for GitHub MCP server
  id: determine-automatic-lockdown
  if: secrets.GH_AW_GITHUB_MCP_SERVER_TOKEN != ''
  uses: actions/github-script@...
  with:
    script: |
      const determineAutomaticLockdown = require('/tmp/gh-aw/actions/determine_automatic_lockdown.cjs');
      await determineAutomaticLockdown(github, context, core);
```

This ensures that:
- The step is always present in the workflow (not conditionally generated at compile time)
- The step only runs at runtime if the custom token secret is defined
- No unnecessary API calls when using the default GITHUB_TOKEN
- The determination is done at runtime based on the actual repository environment

### Documentation Updates

Updated documentation in:
- `docs/src/content/docs/guides/security.md` - Clarified that automatic determination only occurs when `GH_AW_GITHUB_MCP_SERVER_TOKEN` is defined
- `docs/src/content/docs/reference/tools.md` - Updated lockdown field documentation to reflect runtime determination behavior

Key changes:
- Changed "automatically enabled" to "automatically determined" to be more accurate
- Added explicit mention that automatic determination requires `GH_AW_GITHUB_MCP_SERVER_TOKEN`
- Clarified that when using default `GITHUB_TOKEN`, automatic determination is skipped

### Motivation
- Fix a compilation error caused by calling unavailable `hasCustomName()`/`getCustomName()` on `ItemStack` in this environment. 
- Ensure the cleric brewing logic filters and validates ingredients using the server `BrewingRecipeRegistry`. 
- Support multi-stage brewing by recognizing intermediate potion outputs that can be brewed into the final target.

- Replace `stack.hasCustomName()`/`getCustomName()` usage with `stack.get(DataComponentTypes.CUSTOM_NAME)` and check the text via `startsWith(TARGET_POTION_MARKER)` in `isTargetPotionMarker`.

author: bmensah
body:
This PR turns the app into a functional habit tracker for a single day by adding per-habit logging, global daily context, and status showing in the habit list.

### What Changed

1. Daily context: Added DailyContextStore to persist the user's logged barriers to completing their habits fully that day. Made a design simplification for the MVP to have a single, global context for the user to set instead of a specific context for each day.
2. Habit status display: HabitListView now displays a read-only status for each habit based on the user logged tier and the required tier determined by the context. Possible status values are: _Not logged_ (the user has not updated the habit log yet), _Counts as success_ (the user logged tier is greater than or equal to the required tier), and _Below minimum_ (the user logged tier is less than the required tier). Status updates immediately when logging or context changes.

### Validation

- Build succeeds in Xcode
- Logging a tier persists when navigating away and back
- Logging persists after closing app and relaunching the simulator
- Global context persists after closing app and relaunching the simulator
- Habit list shows the correct per-habit status
- No new navigation patterns introduced

### Out of Scope for MVP

- No history added beyond a single day of logging
- No analytics, streaks, or widgets
- No backend or accounts

author: garethbaumgart
body:
## Summary

Fix OAuth redirect_uri mismatch error in Cloud Run deployment.

Cloud Run terminates SSL at the load balancer and forwards requests as HTTP internally. Without forwarded headers support, ASP.NET generates OAuth redirect URIs with `http://` instead of `https://`.

## Changes

- Configure `ForwardedHeadersOptions` to trust `X-Forwarded-For` and `X-Forwarded-Proto` headers
- Add `UseForwardedHeaders()` middleware at the start of the pipeline

## Test plan

- [ ] CI passes
- [ ] OAuth login works on Cloud Run

author: sadocha191
body:
### Motivation
- Ensure the player profile block in the inventory shows the name/level as a bold header first, followed by EXP, race, stats and currencies to match the desired ordering.
- Keep only the player name/level in bold and render the rest of the profile text in the regular font.
- Replace the dot separator with a dash in the name/level header for a consistent header style.

### Description
- Enforced explicit layout ordering by setting `playerName.LayoutOrder = 1`, `expWrap.LayoutOrder = 2`, `raceLabel.LayoutOrder = 3`, and `statsList.LayoutOrder = 4` so elements appear in the requested sequence.
- Kept the name/level label bold and changed its text format to use a dash via `playerName.Text = "%s - Lv. %d"` and updated the runtime formatter in `updatePlayerInfo` accordingly.
- Made the `coinsLabel` use regular font by setting `coinsLabel.Font = Enum.Font.Gotham` so only the header remains bold.
- No gameplay logic was modified; this is a UI-only change scoped to `InventoryController.lua`.

### Testing
- No automated tests were executed for this UI-only change.
- The modification is limited to UI construction and runtime text formatting in `Lobby/StarterPlayer/StarterPlayerScripts/LocalScript/InventoryController.lua`.
- Manual visual verification is recommended to confirm ordering and font styling in the inventory panel.
- No unit or integration tests were added or modified.

author: google-labs-jules[bot]
body:
This PR consolidates the `orion-llamacpp-host` into a single "Introspective Mode" process that handles both Chat and Embeddings on the same port, removing the sidecar embedding server. It also updates the `SignalMapper` in `orion/spark` to lazily initialize the projection matrix, supporting dynamic embedding dimensions (like 4096 for Llama-3) instead of hardcoded 768. Finally, `orion-llm-gateway` settings are updated to default the embedding URL to the chat URL.

author: allmarkedup
body:
Fixes a number issues with previewing Phlex components, as raised in #759

Nested render calls (i.e. within blocks passed to a component) should now work as expected:

```ruby
def nested_rendering_example_scenario
  render Components::SimpleButton.new do
    render Components::SimpleIcon.new
  end
end
```

In addition, calls to Phlex helpers (such as `plain`) within blocks should also now work as expected:

```ruby
def helper_example_scenario
  render Components::SimpleButton.new do
    plain "The button text"
  end
end
```

author: carlossosvos
body:
This pull request introduces a local-first, offline-capable synchronization mechanism for daily logs. It adds a new pending operations table and DAO, updates the repository to enqueue failed remote operations for later sync, and implements a sync routine to flush pending operations. The database schema and migration are updated accordingly.

**Offline sync infrastructure:**

* Added a new `PendingLogSyncOps` table and `PendingLogSyncDao` for tracking local log operations that need to be synchronized with the remote server. Includes schema, DAO, and generated mixin. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-a871746e61034886ea9dc27054ad4adbdd9f9a1c54960f85a3fe00b1eade0789R1-R14) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-ed5ff88e34528f47bc482992c3aac2eac0645484aa4bab9b508c61c5c1b1e1b0R1-R35) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-aba186e31dfd60af66a2db79ac787928cba371eef196abcca8a950a9cb0b551dR1-R9)
* Updated `AppDatabase` to include the new table and DAO, increased the schema version, and added a migration to create the table when upgrading from version 1. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-6e2d1f38e05bc5c7420606568adf551e89055fb2a04e06e4f5ae1ec79c8bf6b9R4-R24) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-6e2d1f38e05bc5c7420606568adf551e89055fb2a04e06e4f5ae1ec79c8bf6b9L25-R35)

**Repository and sync logic:**

* Modified `DailyLogRepositoryImpl` to:
  - Use client-generated temporary IDs for new logs.
  - Enqueue failed create, update, and delete operations in the pending sync table for later retry.
  - On sync, flush all pending operations to the remote server and remove them from the queue on success. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-69a061efd89e682266e641c50e28f43284c533d7251262ee11026731f508805eR13-R19) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-69a061efd89e682266e641c50e28f43284c533d7251262ee11026731f508805eR47-R51) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-69a061efd89e682266e641c50e28f43284c533d7251262ee11026731f508805eR60-R86) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-69a061efd89e682266e641c50e28f43284c533d7251262ee11026731f508805eL114-R128) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-69a061efd89e682266e641c50e28f43284c533d7251262ee11026731f508805eL125-R146) [[6]](diffhunk://#diff-69a061efd89e682266e641c50e28f43284c533d7251262ee11026731f508805eR178-R212)

**Remote datasource adjustments:**

* Updated `DailyLogRemoteDatasource.createLog` to accept an optional `id` parameter, allowing the use of client-generated IDs for offline-created logs. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-90371a9e0c0d0e55616df1e843f122bae372db16bfe09d0e356a63e4b15bdb4cR23) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-90371a9e0c0d0e55616df1e843f122bae372db16bfe09d0e356a63e4b15bdb4cR34)

**Dependency injection:**

* Registered the new `PendingLogSyncDao` in the service locator and injected it into the repository implementation. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-f995de55d9787e9a79d720165352b5104b204dc31d3c6de81e0b308b19a64fcfR36) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-69a061efd89e682266e641c50e28f43284c533d7251262ee11026731f508805eR4)

These changes lay the foundation for robust offline support and reliable data synchronization in the daily log feature.

author: copilot
body:
Smart Mirror widgets were using a single grid layout for all orientations, causing poor arrangement on rotated displays and different aspect ratios.

## Changes

**Data Model** (`modules/smartmirror.js`)
- Separated widget positioning into `layouts.portrait` and `layouts.landscape` objects
- Widget properties (enabled, API keys, etc.) remain shared across orientations
- Added automatic migration from old `gridPosition` format to new dual-layout structure

**API & Routes** (`server.js`)
- Added `/smart-mirror-l` route for landscape-locked displays
- Extended `/api/smart-mirror/config` to accept `?orientation=portrait|landscape` query parameter
- Returns only requested orientation's layout when parameter specified

**Dashboard** (`public/smart-mirror.html`)
- Detects orientation via `window.matchMedia('(orientation: portrait|landscape)')` with fallback to viewport dimensions
- Listens for orientation change events and reloads appropriate layout
- URL-based orientation (`/smart-mirror-l`) locks layout regardless of device rotation

**Admin UI** (`admin/dashboard.html`)
- Added orientation tabs (Portrait/Landscape) to grid editor
- Each orientation editable independently via drag-and-drop interface
- Single save operation persists both layouts
- Preview buttons for each orientation

## Example Config Structure

```javascript
{
  "widgets": {
    "clock": { "enabled": true, "size": "medium" }
  },
  "layouts": {
    "portrait": {
      "clock": { "x": 0, "y": 0, "width": 2, "height": 1 }
    },
    "landscape": {
      "clock": { "x": 0, "y": 0, "width": 1, "height": 1 }
    }
  }
}
```

## Backward Compatibility

Old configs with `gridPosition` in widgets automatically migrate on first load. Migration uses existing positions as defaults for both orientations.

author: splax-s
body:
## Phase 6 Security Hardening

This PR implements three key security features from the roadmap:

### ✅ Capability Revocation Engine
**New file**: `kernel/src/cap/revocation.rs` (~677 lines)

- **RevocationBloomFilter**: O(1) probabilistic revocation checking with configurable false positive rate
- **DelegationChain** tracking: Full provenance from root capability to any derived token
- **DelegationConstraints**: Max delegation depth, time limits, allowed operations, restricted grantees
- **Time-limited capabilities**: Support for Cycles, Milliseconds, Seconds, Minutes, Hours durations
- **RevocationReason enum**: Manual, Expired, ParentRevoked, PolicyViolation, SecurityBreach, OwnerDeleted
- **Cascade revocation**: When a parent capability is revoked, all derived capabilities are automatically revoked
- **Renewal support**: Renewable time-limited tokens can be extended (with max renewal limits)
- **Audit logging**: Full revocation history with timestamps and reasons

### ✅ Secure Key Storage
**New file**: `kernel/src/crypto/keystore.rs` (~728 lines)

- **KeyStore**: Per-process cryptographic key management
- **KeyType**: Master, Symmetric, PrivateKey, PublicKey, Derived, Session
- **KeyAlgorithm**: AES-128/256, ChaCha20, Ed25519, X25519, HMAC-SHA256/512
- **KeyUsage flags**: ENCRYPT, DECRYPT, SIGN, VERIFY, DERIVE, EXPORT, WRAP
- **Key generation**: Hardware RNG-backed secure key generation
- **Key derivation**: HKDF-based key derivation with parent tracking
- **Key rotation**: Predecessor/successor chain for seamless key updates
- **At-rest encryption**: All keys encrypted with ChaCha20-Poly1305
- **Access control**: Per-process ownership, extractable/non-extractable policies
- **Secure cleanup**: KeyMaterial wrapper with automatic zeroization on drop

### Other Changes
- Added `Default` impl for `Operations` (defaults to `NONE`)
- Fixed duplicate module declarations in `crypto/mod.rs`
- Updated ROADMAP.md marking Phase 6 items complete
- Updated CHANGELOG.md with new features

### Testing
- ✅ Kernel builds successfully for x86_64-unknown-none
- ✅ All existing tests pass
- ✅ Boot tested in QEMU

### Roadmap Progress
Completes Phase 6 Security Hardening:
- [x] Capability revocation
- [x] Capability delegation chains
- [x] Time-limited capabilities
- [x] Secure key storage

body:
## Summary
Fixes #132

When a shell process has already exited (user typed `exit`), clicking the close button now closes the tab immediately without showing the confirmation dialog.

## Root Cause
The `closeTab()` function in `dialogs.js` showed a confirmation dialog for all shells and builders, regardless of whether their process was still running. This was confusing for users because when a shell shows "exited" status, asking "Close shell?" implies terminating something that's already dead.

## Fix
1. Added new API endpoint `GET /api/tabs/:tabId/running` in `dashboard-server.ts` that checks if the tab's process is still running using the existing `isProcessRunning()` helper
2. Modified `closeTab()` in `dialogs.js` to call this endpoint before showing the confirmation dialog - if the process has already exited, the tab is closed immediately

## Test Plan
- [x] Added regression tests for the new API endpoint
- [x] Added test verifying closeTab checks running status
- [x] TypeScript compiles without errors
- [x] Net diff is 89 LOC (under 300 LOC threshold)

### Motivation
- Enforce secure token handling: single active refresh token per user, rotation on refresh, and mass invalidation on logout/password/role change.
- Make RBAC canonical and strict with typed roles, deny-by-default guards, and audit of access-denied events.
- Prevent runtime schema creation by adding versioned migrations and fail startup/readiness if migrations are pending.
- Improve security observability and protections with rate limiting, account lockout, request IDs, and normalized errors.

### Description
- Add `migrations/001_init.sql` and a migration runner `src/migrations.ts` with `runMigrations`, `getPendingMigrations`, and `assertNoPendingMigrations`, and wire checks into `initializeServer` and `/api/_int/ready`.
- Harden auth: add `token_version` to users, include `tokenVersion` in access/refresh payloads, generate a `tokenId` for refresh tokens, rotate refresh tokens on refresh, enforce single active refresh token by deleting existing tokens before insert, and revoke/increment `token_version` on logout/password/role change via new repo helpers (`incrementTokenVersion`, `revokeRefreshTokensForUser`).
- RBAC and types: replace string literals with a single `ROLES` constant and `Role` type, add `isRole` validation, change `requireRole` to accept `readonly Role[]`, and record an `access_denied` audit event when denial occurs.
- Security & ops: add `requestLogger` middleware with `x-request-id` support, add `passwordResetRateLimit`, keep existing `loginRateLimit`/`refreshRateLimit`, implement account lockout using `failed_login_attempts` and `locked_until`, and normalize/emit server error logs in `errorHandler`.
- CI / build: update `jest.config.cjs` for CI stability, and update GitHub Actions workflow to validate required env vars and run `npm test` before `npm run build` and verify `dist` output.

### Testing
- Ran unit/e2e tests with `npm test` and all tests passed (`13 passed, 13 total`), including `src/__tests__/auth.test.ts` which verifies login → refresh → revoke, RBAC, lockout, and token invalidation flows.

body:
Refines the `PageLayout.Pane` resizable persistence API with clearer configuration types and simplified custom persistence functions based on design review feedback.

### Changes

**Type Structure**
- Split `PersistConfig` into three distinct types:
  - `NoPersistConfig`: `{persist: false}` - SSR-safe, no width control
  - `LocalStoragePersistConfig`: `{persist: 'localStorage', widthStorageKey: string, width: number | undefined}` - explicit storage key in config
  - `CustomPersistConfig`: `{persist: fn, width: number | undefined}` - consumer manages storage
- `width` is required (can be `undefined`) for persistence configs to ensure intentional state management
- Added type guards: `isNoPersistConfig`, `isLocalStoragePersistConfig`, `isCustomPersistConfig`

**Custom Persist Functions**
- Simplified signature: `(width: number) => void | Promise<void>`
- No longer receives `widthStorageKey` - consumers manage their own storage keys
- `SaveOptions` type is now empty

**Deprecations**
- `widthStorageKey` prop marked `@deprecated` - use config object instead
- `resizable={true}` implicitly deprecated - use explicit config
- Backwards compatibility maintained

**Migration Examples**

Before (deprecated):
```tsx
<PageLayout.Pane resizable={true} widthStorageKey="my-pane" />

<PageLayout.Pane
  resizable={{
    persist: (width, {widthStorageKey}) => storage.set(widthStorageKey, width)
  }}
  widthStorageKey="my-key"
/>
```

After:
```tsx
<PageLayout.Pane 
  resizable={{
    persist: 'localStorage',
    widthStorageKey: 'my-pane',
    width: undefined
  }} 
/>

<PageLayout.Pane
  resizable={{
    persist: (width) => storage.set('my-key', width),
    width: currentWidth
  }}
/>
```

SSR-safe (no persistence):
```tsx
<PageLayout.Pane resizable={{persist: false}} />
```

### Changelog

#### New

- `NoPersistConfig`, `LocalStoragePersistConfig`, `CustomPersistConfig` types
- Type guards for each config type
- Migration examples story in Storybook

#### Changed

- `PersistFunction` signature: no longer receives options parameter
- `widthStorageKey` moved into `LocalStoragePersistConfig` from prop-only
- `width` now required (can be `undefined`) for persistence configs
- `SaveOptions` is now an empty object

#### Removed

- `SaveOptions` from public exports (internal only)

### Rollout strategy

- [ ] Patch release
- [x] Minor release
- [ ] Major release; if selected, include a written rollout or migration plan
- [ ] None; if selected, include a brief description as to why

Minor release with deprecation warnings. Breaking changes deferred to next major version. Backwards compatibility maintained via fallback to `widthStorageKey` prop when `resizable={true}`.

### Testing & Reviewing

- 86 unit tests covering all new types and migration paths
- Type guards validated for all config variants
- Backwards compatibility with `resizable={true}` tested
- Storybook examples demonstrate migration patterns

### Merge checklist

- [x] Added/updated tests
- [x] Added/updated documentation
- [x] Added/updated previews (Storybook)
- [x] Changes are [SSR compatible](https://github.com/primer/react/blob/main/contributor-docs/CONTRIBUTING.md#ssr-compatibility)
- [ ] Tested in Chrome

<details>

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

## Summary

Refine the `PageLayout.Pane` resizable persistence API based on design review feedback. This builds on the existing work in the `make-primer-react-pagelayout-accept-persister` branch.

## API Changes

### New Type Definitions

Update the types in `packages/react/src/PageLayout/usePaneWidth.ts`:

```tsx
/**
 * Options passed to custom persist function.
 * Note: widthStorageKey is no longer passed - custom persisters manage their own storage.
 */
export type SaveOptions = {}

/**
 * Custom persist function type.
 * Receives the width value; consumer manages their own storage key/mechanism.
 */
export type PersistFunction = (width: number) => void | Promise<void>

/**
 * No persistence - SSR safe, uses default width from width prop.
 * width is not allowed here - always uses default.
 */
export type NoPersistConfig = {
  persist: false
}

/**
 * localStorage persistence - requires explicit storage key.
 * width is REQUIRED (can be undefined to use default).
 */
export type LocalStoragePersistConfig = {
  persist: 'localStorage'
  /** Storage key for localStorage. Required to avoid key collisions. */
  widthStorageKey: string
  /** Current controlled width value. Required - use undefined for "use default". */
  width: number | undefined
}

/**
 * Custom persistence - consumer handles storage.
 * width is REQUIRED (can be undefined to use default).
 */
export type CustomPersistConfig = {
  persist: PersistFunction
  /** Current controlled width value. Required - use undefined for "use default". */
  width: number | undefined
}

export type PersistConfig = NoPersistConfig | LocalStoragePersistConfig | CustomPersistConfig

/**
 * Resizable configuration options.
 * - `true`: Enable resizing with default localStorage persistence (DEPRECATED - use {persist: 'localStorage', widthStorageKey, width} instead)
 * - `false`: Disable resizing
 * - `{persist: false}`: Enable resizing without persistence (SSR-safe)
 * - `{persist: 'localStorage', widthStorageKey, width}`: Enable with localStorage, width required
 * - `{persist: fn, width}`: Enable with custom persistence, width required
 */
export type ResizableConfig = boolean | PersistConfig
```

### Usage Examples

```tsx
// Disable resizing
resizable={false}

// No persistence - SSR safe, simple
resizable={{persist: false}}

// localStorage - widthStorageKey required, width required (undefined = use default)
resizable={{persist: 'localStorage', widthStorageKey: 'my-pane-width', width: undefined}}
resizable={{persist: 'localStorage', widthStorageKey: 'my-pane-width', width: currentWidth}}

// Custom persistence - width required (undefined = use default)
resizable={{persist: (width) => saveToServer(width), width: undefined}}
resizable={{persist: (width) => setCurrentWidth(width), width: currentWidth}}

// DEPRECATED: Legacy boolean true still works with widthStorageKey prop
<PageLayout.Pane resizable={true} widthStorageKey="my-pane" />
```

### Deprecation Strategy

1. **Deprecate `widthStorageKey` prop on `PageLayout.Pane`**:
   - Add `@deprecated` JSDoc annotation
   - Implementation should prefer `resizable.widthStorageKey` (for localStorage config), falling back to the prop for backwards compatibility with `resizable={true}`

2. **`resizable={true}` is implicitly deprecated**:
   - Still works for backwards compatibility
   - Uses `widthStorageKey` prop (with default fallback)
   - Document migration path to `{persist: 'localStorage', widthStorageKey: '...', width: undefined}`

### Implementation Changes

1. **Update `usePaneWidth.ts`**:
   - Update type definitions as shown above
   - Add type guards: `isLocalStoragePersistConfig`, `isCustomPersistConfig`, `isNoPersistConfig`
   - Update `saveWidth` to not pass `widthStorageKey` to custom persist functions
   - Handle `widthStorageKey` from config for localStorage persist
   - For `resizable === true`, fall back to `widthStorageKey` from hook options (prop)

2. **Update `PageLayout.tsx`**:
   - Add `@deprecated` to `widthStorageKey` prop JSDoc
   - Pass `widthStorageKey` prop to hook for backwards compatibility

3. **Update `PageLayout/index.ts`**:
   - Export new types: `NoPersistConfig`, `LocalStoragePersistConfig`, `CustomPersistConfig`
   - Remove `SaveOptions` export (no longer needed externally)

4. **Update `.changeset/pagelayout-resizable-persistence.md`**:
   - Document the refined API
   - Include migration examples

Implement user information display on the home page by parsing authentication data from secure cookies server-side, replacing the insecure x-backend-session header pattern.

## Changes

**New server-side session utility** (`lib/security/session-utils.ts`)
- `getBackendSession()` extracts `BackendSession` from HTTP-only cookies using Next.js `cookies()` API
- Parses JWT access token and user info cookie set during OAuth callback
- Returns `null` for unauthenticated requests

**New UserInfo component** (`components/user-info.tsx`)
- Displays user name, email, and profile picture in fixed top-right position
- Falls back to avatar with initial when picture unavailable
- Pure presentational component receiving props from layout

**Updated root layout** (`app/layout.tsx`)
- Changed to async server component
- Calls `getBackendSession()` and conditionally renders `UserInfo`

**Removed x-backend-session header**
- Deleted all middleware logic that created and attached session data to request/response headers
- Simplified authenticated request flow to `return NextResponse.next()`
- Updated test to verify authenticated requests proceed without checking header

## Example

```tsx
// Root layout extracts session server-side
export default async function RootLayout({ children }) {
  const session = await getBackendSession();
  
  return (
    <body>
      {session && (
        <UserInfo
          name={session.authenticatedUser.name}
          email={session.authenticatedUser.email}
          picture={session.authenticatedUser.picture}
        />
      )}
      {children}
    </body>
  );
}
```

author: stephenberry
body:
# Runtime BEVE/CBOR Constraints

Adds support for runtime constraints when reading BEVE and CBOR formats. This complements the existing compile-time constraints (used with `glz::meta` and `max_length_t`).

## Changes

### `include/glaze/core/context.hpp`

Added three concepts to detect runtime constraint fields in user-defined contexts:

- `has_runtime_max_string_length`
- `has_runtime_max_array_size`
- `has_runtime_max_map_size`

### `include/glaze/beve/read.hpp`

Added runtime constraint checks at 9 locations (strings, arrays, maps) using `if constexpr` with the new concepts.

### `include/glaze/cbor/read.hpp`

Added runtime constraint checks at 7 locations (strings, arrays, maps) using `if constexpr` with the new concepts.

## Usage

Users inherit from `glz::context` and add constraint fields:

```cpp
struct my_context : glz::context {
   size_t max_string_length = 0;  // 0 = no limit
   size_t max_array_size = 0;
   size_t max_map_size = 0;
};

my_context ctx;
ctx.max_array_size = user_provided_limit;  // Set dynamically at runtime

glz::read<glz::opts{.format = glz::BEVE}>(output, buffer, ctx);
```

## Design

- **Zero binary overhead**: Uses `if constexpr` with concepts, so code is compiled out when using the base `glz::context`
- **Additive**: Runtime constraints work alongside compile-time constraints; either can reject
- **Consistent**: Same field names and semantics as compile-time options (0 = no limit)

Closes #2198

body:
Addresses all review comments from the copilot-pull-request-reviewer bot on PR #69's LLM chat feature.

## Backend
- **UUID validation**: `conversation_id` path parameter now validated before lookup
- **System message deduplication**: Filter stored system messages to prevent conflicts with injected system prompt
- **Empty response handling**: Mark queue items as failed instead of persisting empty assistant messages
- **Worker lifecycle**: Start worker when `loading=True` (previously only when `enabled=True`)
- **Code cleanup**: Remove redundant null check after guaranteed assignment

## Frontend
- **Polling optimization**: Reduce interval from 2s to 5s
- **React hooks**: Wrap `refreshStatus` and `loadConversation` with `useCallback`, add to dependency arrays

## Tests
Added 10 test functions covering:
- `/api/dashboard/llm_chat` structure and behavior
- `/api/llm_chat/enable` endpoint
- `/api/llm_chat/send` validation, conversation management, worker lifecycle
- `/api/llm_chat/conversations/{id}` UUID validation and 404 handling
- `_build_chat_messages` system message filtering

Example of system message fix:
```python
def _build_chat_messages(conversation: dict[str, Any], user_content: str) -> list[dict[str, str]]:
    messages: list[dict[str, str]] = []
    if _CHAT_SYSTEM_PROMPT:
        messages.append({"role": MessageRole.SYSTEM.value, "content": _CHAT_SYSTEM_PROMPT})
    for msg in conversation.get("messages") or []:
        role = msg.get("role")
        content = msg.get("content")
        # Skip system messages from history to avoid conflicts with prepended system prompt
        if role in _CHAT_ROLES and content and role != MessageRole.SYSTEM.value:
            messages.append({"role": role, "content": str(content)})
    messages.append({"role": MessageRole.USER.value, "content": user_content})
    return messages
```

author: damonc0313
body:
### Motivation
- Provide a runtime-executor to implement the read → process → write state-update cycle against the SQLite substrate. 
- Ensure identity, sovereignty, and viability are read from the substrate so behavior follows database-defined constraints. 
- Make operator inputs auditable and actionable by appending explicit `ledger` rows that capture observations and next actions. 
- Replace the previous agent instructions with the supplied cognitive-architecture protocol to centralize operator guidance.

### Description
- Add `driver.py` that loads the SQL substrate into an in-memory SQLite DB and exposes bootstrap (`master_bootstrap`), procedure selection (`select_procedures`), input processing (`process_input`), and ledger append (`append_ledger_insert`) logic. 
- Enforce sovereignty and viability checks by consulting `activation_keys` and `viability_metrics` and selecting procedures based on momentum text and stored `procedures`. 
- Format and append `INSERT INTO "ledger"` statements (observation, next_action, confidence, etc.) directly to the SQL substrate file via `append_ledger_insert`. 
- Overwrite `AGENTS.md` with the provided "COGNITIVE ARCHITECTURE: NEOCORTICAL SEPARATION" protocol and add three operator-input ledger rows (`C130-INPUT`, `C131-INPUT`, `C132-INPUT`) to the substrate SQL file.

### Testing
- Executed `python driver.py` which bootstrapped from `master_bootstrap`, printed identity/mode/viability and processed input, and exited with code 0. 
- Ran small SQLite inspections (selecting from `procedures`, `activation_keys`, and `viability_metrics`) to confirm procedure selection and presence of `ak-sovereignty`, which returned the expected rows. 
- Verified that running the driver produced formatted `INSERT INTO "ledger"` appends to the substrate file (the new `C130-INPUT`–`C132-INPUT` rows are present).
